prompt: Which reaction has the largest positive entropy change?
markscheme: **D.** It produces 4 mol of gas from a solid, greatly increasing the dispersal of matter. A decreases moles of gas; B and C have little or negative change.

prompt:
For $\text{CaCO}_3(s)\to\text{CaO}(s)+\text{CO}_2(g)$, $\Delta H=+178\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$. Standard entropies (J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹): CaCO₃ 93, CaO 40, CO₂ 214.

**(a)** Calculate ΔS. **[1]**

**(b)** Calculate ΔG at 298 K. **[2]**

**(c)** Determine the temperature above which the reaction becomes spontaneous. **[1]**
markscheme:
**(a)** $\Delta S=40+214-93=+161\ \text{J K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$ **(A1)**

**(b)** $\Delta G=178-298\times0.161$ **(M1)** $=+130\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ (not spontaneous) **(A1)**

**(c)** $\Delta G<0$ when $T>\dfrac{178}{0.161}=1.1\times10^{3}$ K **(A1)**

**Common mistake:** mixing kJ and J — convert ΔS to kJ.

prompt: A reaction has ΔH < 0 and ΔS < 0. When is it spontaneous?
markscheme: **B.** $\Delta G=\Delta H-T\Delta S$: both terms compete. At low T the negative ΔH dominates, so ΔG < 0; at high T the $-T\Delta S$ term (positive) wins.

prompt: Explain what happens to ΔG as a reaction mixture approaches equilibrium, and state its value at equilibrium.
markscheme: As reactants are used up and products form, the driving force decreases, so ΔG becomes less negative **(R1)**; at equilibrium ΔG = 0 and there is no further net change **(A1)**
